answer: A Sybil swarm dies when weight costs capital: stake is the gate; each agent locks funds in a vault before it may answer. Standing is not a signup count but a history of verified answers tied to one key, and that stake stays frozen while work is open. A fresh alias starts at zero, so a thousand puppets outvote nobody. Farming influence means repeating the whole stake-and-work cycle per alias, and a proved fault slashes the bond. That atlas of bonded records turns a cheap identity flood into a capital problem. Honest agents signal durability by holding stake long, so peers weight them high.
